source.title: CiteSure: retrieval-augmented large language models for faithful biomedical citation recommendation

source_reconciliation.supplements: No supplementary material was included in the uploaded PDF.

extraction_warnings.message: Methods state that fabricated citations receive relevance score 0 and that mean relevance is computed across all citations, but Table 2 reports standalone-LLM relevance denominators only among factually accurate citations (for example 278/412 rather than 278/2525). Table 2 values were extracted exactly and labeled as Table 2 relevance scores.

The Results text says human annotators cross-referenced Medline and Google Scholar, whereas the Table 1 footnote defines factual accuracy using PubMed verification. Both descriptions were preserved in provenance and validation notes.
Methods list Recall, MAP, MRR, and Precision@5 for reranking evaluation, but Table 3 provides only MAP, MRR, and Precision@5. No Recall atom was created.
Figure 2 provides curves rather than exact tabulated values. Only the text-supported statement that BioLLM2Vec exceeded 80% at top 100 was extracted; no values were estimated from pixels.
The main benchmark tables do not report confidence intervals, variance, or formal significance tests. These fields remain absent rather than inferred.

schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated fields for AI model, dataset split, benchmark, or compute configuration; model systems were represented using ExposureDescriptor and method statements.
The quantitative schema represents one estimate per atom, so each table metric was extracted as a separate independently reviewable atom.
The schema cannot directly encode inequalities such as 'over 80%'; the Figure 2 result was retained as a qualitative_result atom with the reported threshold in the canonical statement.
Publication-level metadata are not part of LiteratureAtom and were emitted in a separate source-metadata JSON file.
extraction_limitations: Atoms were extracted from the uploaded article PDF only; linked repositories, datasets, code, and supplementary materials were not inspected.
All atoms remain review_status=needs_review because no human verification step was performed.
The extraction records reported study content and does not convert independent appraisal into reported data.
No missing confidence intervals, p-values, dataset splits, or unreported metric values were invented.
